blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Classpath code calls setAccessible(true) on a private field of a class whose package, in a named module, is not opened to it. What happens?

options.text: The setAccessible call throws InaccessibleObjectException, an unchecked exception.
options.says: The module check is made when access is requested, and a package that is not opened refuses deep reflection with InaccessibleObjectException, a RuntimeException.

options.text: The setAccessible call returns, and the later get throws IllegalAccessException.
options.says: IllegalAccessException is what using a member without lifted access throws; in a closed package the lifting itself already fails.

options.text: The setAccessible call returns, and the field reads normally from then on.
options.says: Only an opens directive or an --add-opens flag grants deep reflection into a named module's package.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: Code evaluates the class literal Config.class for the first time, and Config has a static block. What does the JVM do with Config?

options.text: It loads Config and runs the static block, as Class.forName(name) does.
options.says: Running the static initializer is what forName's default variant adds; a class literal never initializes the class.

options.text: It does nothing at run time, since javac already resolved the literal.
options.says: The literal is checked at compile time, but the class still has to be loaded the first time the literal is evaluated at run time.

options.text: It loads Config if needed, and the static block has not run afterwards.
options.says: A class literal may load the class the first time it is evaluated but does not initialize it, so the static block waits for the first active use.

concepts: A class literal may load its class the first time it is evaluated but never runs the static initializer.
setAccessible(true) on a member of a named module's package that is not opened to the caller throws InaccessibleObjectException.
